run.title: Three White Lights
run.subtitle: Gauntlet Loop build run
run.waveName: Wave 2 — closing math send-backs; art started

blockers.title: Run halted once on the subagent spend limit, now resumed
blockers.body: Six agents were killed mid-flight when the monthly limit was hit: two critics, the e1RM rework, and the fatigue, streak and sprite builders. No usable work was lost — neither partially-started builder had committed anything, and their worktrees were discarded.
blockers.consequence: Dispatch is working again. The queue resumed in priority order: close the e1RM send-back first, then grade the two modules that were merged but never judged. The art and UI half of the run still has not started.

blockers.title: Reference material cannot be retrieved in this sandbox
blockers.body: Egress policy allows the npm registry and GitHub, and WebSearch returns text results. Everything else — Wikipedia/Wikimedia, openpowerlifting.org, sprite archives, image hosts — is refused at the proxy with a 403 on CONNECT. No image, video, or PDF reference can be fetched.
blockers.consequence: Every GDD §12.2 bar that requires blind A/B against real reference art is structurally unverifiable here: lifter sprites, gym/environment art, result card vs. real federation sheets, anime cut-ins, and meet-day tension vs. broadcast footage. Per CLAUDE.md these are reported unverifiable rather than passed on reasoning alone. More loop rounds cannot fix this — it needs reference files supplied locally.

blockers.title: GDD §6.3 contradicts CLAUDE.md on decreasing attempt weight
blockers.body: CLAUDE.md states attempts may not go down in weight within a lift. GDD §6.3 offers, after a miss, to "repeat the weight … vs. drop down (guaranteed banked total, no PR)". Both cannot hold.
blockers.consequence: Real-sport rules side with CLAUDE.md — within a lift a weight may be repeated after a miss but never decreased — so the meet engine enforces non-decreasing and the conflict is flagged rather than silently resolved. If §6.3's "drop down" meant taking a smaller jump rather than going below the last attempt, the GDD wording needs updating; if it meant a real decrease, that is a deliberate departure from the sport and the engine needs changing. Your call — CLAUDE.md forbids me picking one quietly.

blockers.title: CLAUDE.md names Epley/Brzycki; the e1RM fix now leads with the RPE chart
blockers.body: CLAUDE.md's Domain Correctness rule says e1RM should use "an established formula (Epley or Brzycki)". Closing the e1RM send-back meant making the estimate RPE-aware, and the cleanest published route was the Tuchscherer chart itself — its own structure already collapses to one curve over effective rep max. Epley is gone; Brzycki survives only past the chart's coverage.
blockers.consequence: Both remedies the critic named led here, and GDD §12.2 lists "published RPE charts" alongside e1RM formulas, so nothing homebrewed is involved — but it is a judgement call about which published source dominates, and it departs from CLAUDE.md's literal wording. Flagged rather than settled. Either CLAUDE.md's e1RM sentence needs widening, or the chart-first approach needs reverting.

pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: THE GRID WINS ITS BAR ON VALUES — a critic re-fetched both pinned sources and checked all 108 cells, and verified byte-for-byte that the committed fixtures had not been reformatted by the refactor. The remaining gap is an inconsistency: the module argues at length that compile-time readonly is not enough and freezes the chart, the sources and the provenance record — but leaves the three objects that GATE the lookup unfrozen. Verified here: pushing 7.3 onto CHARTED_RPES makes isChartedRpe(7.3) true and tryPercentOf1RM returns undefined, which is neither number nor null. The quieter variant produces no error at all — shifting MAX_RPE by half a step moves every prescribed load and every e1RM while all 66 tests stay green. The provenance footnotes are protected from mutation; the definition of which RPEs exist is not.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: Graded: mathematics verified sound by hand — RPE moves the estimate correctly, RIR substitution applied consistently, composite curve strictly increasing, seam continuous, no invented values anywhere. Failed only on auditability: the header quoted chart figures that had gone stale, which I introduced when merging the chart fix and have now corrected, along with an inverted inequality the critic also caught in my correction.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR — the only piece to be graded and pass. All ten coefficients verified by the critic against source bytes it fetched itself from OpenPowerlifting, term order checked by hand two ways. Noted gap: no test pins any DOTS value to anything outside the repo, so a wrong digit at authoring time could not fail the suite.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Structure WINS ITS BAR. Rework 5 merged: the rules-seal subsystem is gone — four constants, a unique-symbol brand, an error code, an exported check, four call sites, a 41-line essay and nine tests, including the BigInt re-derivation blind to the digits it was meant to check. Rules are now opaque behind a module-private symbol, so the tampering spread does not type-check, and the guard is proven by negative controls that revert it and confirm the directives go unused. meet.ts is 51 lines shorter and has no arithmetic left to get wrong.

pieces.name: Lifter sprites & animation
pieces.bar: Blind A/B against real 16-bit SNES/Genesis sprite work. Maximal attempt must animate heavier.
pieces.note: Half the bar UNVERIFIABLE (no reference retrievable), half SENT BACK. The timing model genuinely clears "not merely slower" — ascent shape in normalised time, stall at the authored height, bar-path divergence, all quantified and load-monotone. But the heaviness is carried by the barbell and the clock, not the lifter. Both loads walk the same eleven authored poses; the critic did the arithmetic and found the light rep peaks at strain level 1 and the maximal at 3, giving body deltas of 0.6-1.6px on a 60px figure — several of which will not survive rounding. Confirmed by eye on the pose sheet: strain rows 1 and 2 are indistinguishable, and 3-4 separate mainly by an open-mouth grimace and a ruddier skin ramp. Strip the bar out and the two lifters are the same drawing. Also: the forward-drift term is clamped away on heavy reps so it only ever changes the LIGHT rep, and the strongest pixel test compares strain 0 vs 3 — levels the animation never produces — asserting only that something differs.

pieces.name: Cross-module inconsistency (found, unfixed)
pieces.bar: The four modes must feel like one game — the smoothing-pass concern.
pieces.note: The DOTS critic caught it while grading something else: meet.ts models a bomb-out as total: null, dots.ts assumes 0. The meet-engine critic then adjudicated it independently — meet.ts is right, since a lifter with no total does not place, so dots.ts is the module that should change. Not yet fixed.
